newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Wide spread limits interest.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Wide spread limits interest.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market held steady as buyers were turned off by high offers and pressure to widen the spread between 180-cst and 380-cst, traders said on Tuesday.
Centistoke 180 supplies for March loading were offered at between $99.00-$99.50 per tonne. One seller lowered his offer later to $97.00 but there were no takers.
Most traders were sidelined by the wide spread between 180 cst and 380-cst quotes. They said a $9.00 per tonne differential reflected in Singapore published quotes was not realistic.
"At maximum, the spread should be at around $6 per tonne," said one trader.
Most players were adopting a wait and see stance, hoping to get a clearer market direction before moving any cargoes.
Sources said the wide spread between the two grades was caused by a trader putting pressure on price assessments as he brings in 380-cst supplies from Mideast.
Late Thursday, a 380-cst cargo was heard traded at $90 per tonne while talks on 180-cst supplies hovered around $99, traders said.

Traders said in the medium term, the return of Chinese demand will help to pull prices out of their doldrums. Supplies from South Korea and Jappan were expected to remain unchanged from previous months.

In the LSWR market, traders said the completion of a turnround schedule in Pertamina's 120,000 bpd Dumai refinery is expected to reduce Indonesia's allocation in March. This would help support prices, said one trader.
